samples.summary: `Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection` — the entire cross-tab undo landing path — has no test
samples.evidence: `focusUndoSelection` contains real branching (row → selectRow/selectRowRange, column → selectColumn/selectColumnRange, cell → selectStart/selectEnd only when the range is not a single cell, plus render/reveal/notify). Grepping the repo for `focusUndoSelection` returns only its definition (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:689) and its single call site (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1454) — no test file mentions it. The two new sheets test files cover `resolveUndoSelection` and `Sheet.applyUndoSelection`, but nothing exercises the view-level restore, which is the only code that makes a cross-tab undo visible to the user. A defect here (e.g. off-by-one in the `end.r > start.r` guard, or the cell branch leaving a stale multi-range) ships silently.

samples.summary: The `merges` operation branch of `collectTouches` is untested
samples.evidence: `case 'merges'` parses `op.key` with `parseRef` and pushes it into `touch.cells` (undo-selection.ts:197-205), including a swallowed parse failure. Neither new test file contains an op with a `.merges` path (grep for `merges` in packages/sheets/test/workbook/undo-selection.test.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-undo.test.ts: 0 hits). The old `computeAffectedRange` this replaces explicitly diffed merges, so merge-undo selection is a behavior that regressed out of coverage; a wrong key format would leave undo-of-merge selecting nothing and nothing would fail.

samples.summary: `rowStyles` / `colStyles` op paths are untested; only `rowHeights` / `colWidths` are
samples.evidence: The switch handles four axis-keyed fields (rowHeights, rowStyles, colWidths, colStyles) at undo-selection.ts:206-217, but the unit test only feeds `rowHeights` (test line 158) and `colWidths` (line 146). Grep for `rowStyles`/`colStyles` in packages/sheets/test/workbook/undo-selection.test.ts: no matches. Undoing a whole-row/column style change would then select nothing and no test would notice.

samples.summary: The `rangeStyles` path is only tested with fabricated patches cast through `as any`, never end-to-end through a real store
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/test/workbook/undo-selection.test.ts:169-274 builds RangeStylePatch literals cast `as any` (lines 180, 206, 241-242, 270), so the test cannot detect a mismatch between the real patch shape produced by `cloneRangeStylePatch` in YorkieStore.snapshotTabs and what `diffRangeStyles` JSON-stringifies/reads (`patch.range`). yorkie-store-undo.test.ts contains no style operation at all (grep for `style`: 0 hits), even though it exercises every other kind of edit against a real Yorkie document. Styling a range and undoing it is a common user path whose selection could be wrong with the suite green.

samples.summary: The React cross-tab jump wiring (request-id dedup, tab filter, clearing on history reset) has no test
samples.evidence: The new effect at sheet-view.tsx:1443-1455 guards on tabId match and `lastHandledUndoJumpRequestIdRef`, and document-detail.tsx:177 clears `undoJumpTarget` on a revision restore — the task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260917-sheets-undo-selection-todo.md:169) records 'A pending undoJumpTarget survived a revision restore' as a real defect found here. No frontend test references `undoJumpTarget`/`handleUndoJump` (grep across repo returns only source and docs). The only new frontend test, yorkie-store-undo.test.ts, tests the store, not the wiring. A regression re-applying a stale jump after a restore would be user-visible and uncaught.

samples.summary: Mixed row+column touches and the multi-other-tab weight tiebreak fall through untested
samples.evidence: `resolveUndoSelection` only emits a row/column header selection when the other axis set is empty (lines 444, 456); a step touching both rowHeights and colWidths silently yields a selection with no range. No test covers that combination. Likewise `pickTab`'s max-weight branch (lines 246-249) is only exercised with a single non-current tab (test 'reports another tab so the editor can switch to it'), so a broken comparison between two foreign tabs would not be caught.
searchedFor: grep colWidths/rowHeights combinations in that test

samples.summary: The new scroll-to-selection on undo/redo (`revealActiveCell`) is not asserted anywhere
samples.evidence: spreadsheet.ts:655 and :667 add `this.worksheet.revealActiveCell()` after undo/redo, and worksheet.ts:558 adds the method. No test in packages/sheets/test/view/* references `revealActiveCell`; the new Sheet-level tests operate below the view. Failure mode is cosmetic (undo lands off-screen), hence nit.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection` exists at packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:689-707 with three real branches and conditional guards (`end.r > start.r`, `end.c > start.c`, single-cell check) plus render/reveal/notify. A case-insensitive repo-wide grep for `focusUndo|UndoTabJump` (excluding .agent-review) yields only the definition, the sole call site at packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1454, the registration plumbing, docs, and one test hit at packages/sheets/test/sheet/undo-selection.test.ts:191 which is `setOnUndoTabJump` (the model-level reporting callback), not the view restore. I searched beyond the reviewer's paths: the full packages/sheets/test tree including test/view/ (14 files), all 246 frontend test files, and every *.test.ts(x)/*.spec.ts in the repo matching "undo" (88 files); no e2e dir exists. The two new test files import only model code (MemStore/Sheet, resolveUndoSelection) and never import src/view/spreadsheet. Crucially, the repo already has a cheap, established pattern for exactly this kind of test — packages/sheets/test/view/spreadsheet-readonly-recalc.test.ts:23-45 invokes a Spreadsheet.prototype method against a hand-built {sheet, worksheet, _readOnly} context — so the branching in focusUndoSelection is trivially testable and simply untested. Major: this is the only code that makes a cross-tab undo landing visible to the user, so an off-by-one in the range guards or a stale multi-range from the cell branch would ship undetected on a user-facing path.
